$comment: Generated by scripts/generate-mercury-field-enum-reference.mjs — do not edit by hand. apiValidated:false means the contract types the field as a plain string; the values are a catalog, not a constraint.

controlRules.rationale: ≤3 options — show them all, no click to discover them
4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
13–60 options — needs type-to-filter, but the full list is still renderable
>60 options — filter-as-you-type only; never render the full list

enums.name: AuState
enums.label: State / territory
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: The list is 9 long, not 8: it carries an explicit `OTHER` alongside the eight AU states and territories. On `Identification.placeOfIssue`, `OTHER` is how an interstate or overseas issuing authority is recorded — a picker limited to the real states silently cannot express those documents.

enums.name: Frequency
enums.label: Frequency (Title Case)
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: Mercury carries two frequency enums that are not interchangeable. This one is Title Case and uses `Annual`; `FrequencyLower` is lowercase and uses `annually`. Sharing one frequency control across Expense/Income and Asset/Liability requires mapping both the casing *and* the word — `Annual` → `annually` is not a `toLowerCase()`.

enums.name: FrequencyLower
enums.label: Frequency (lowercase)
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: Lowercase variant used by every Asset and Liability frequency field. `annually`, not `annual` — the odd one out if you derive it from `Frequency` by lowercasing.

enums.name: AssetLiabilityType
enums.label: Asset / liability type
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: This is the enum that drives conditional form sections, not just a value: `realEstate` reveals the `address` + `realEstate*` + `existingMortgage*` groups, `vehicle` reveals `motorVehicle*`, `account` reveals `accountName`/`accountNumber`/`accountBSB`, and `standard` reveals nothing beyond `details`.

It has to stay consistent with `Asset.name` / `Liability.name`, which is a separate enum — picking the name `Real Estate` and the type `vehicle` is representable on the wire and meaningless downstream.

enums.name: CountryCode
enums.label: Country
enums.controlRationale: >60 options — filter-as-you-type only; never render the full list
hazards: 250 codes — typeahead only.
It is not the current ISO 3166-1 list: `AN` (Netherlands Antilles, withdrawn 2010) is present. Validating user input against a live ISO library will reject values Mercury itself accepts and returns.
The original Swagger had Norway's `NO` parsed as the boolean `false` (unquoted YAML). This live-audited contract has it fixed — but any client generated from the older spec still carries the bug.

enums.name: ContactTitle
enums.label: Title
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance

enums.name: MaritalStatus
enums.label: Marital status
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: `DeFacto` is one unspaced word on the wire. Display it as “De Facto” by all means, but the value you send back is `DeFacto`.

enums.name: Gender
enums.label: Gender
enums.controlRationale: ≤3 options — show them all, no click to discover them
hazards: The wire contract admits exactly `M` and `F`. There is no non-binary, other, or undisclosed value, so a form cannot offer one — anything else is rejected. The field is optional, so leaving it unset is the honest representation of “not one of these two”; don't force a choice to satisfy the control.

enums.name: EmploymentStatusContact
enums.label: Employment status (Contact)
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: Name collision: `Contact.employmentStatus` is this 9-value enum (Full Time, Casual, Self-Employed …), while `Employment.employmentStatus` on the nested Employment record is free text carrying a completely different vocabulary (Primary, Secondary, Previous). Same field name, different entity, different meaning — do not bind both to one control.

enums.name: PhoneDisplayType
enums.label: Phone slot type
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: Four parallel fields (`phoneDisplayType1`…`4`) share this one enum. They are slots, so the same value in two slots is a data-entry error the API will happily store — de-duplicate the selected value across the four controls.

enums.name: ContactMethodEnum
enums.label: Contact method slot
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: Sits on the same record as `ContactMethod.type` and must stay coherent with it: `Email 1/2/3` go with type `email`, `Mobile`/`Mobile 2` with `mobile`, `Home`/`Home 2`/`Home Fax` with `home`, and the `Business*` values with `phone`. That pairing is inferred from the value names and matching live payloads — it is not asserted by the contract, so derive `type` from the slot but let it be overridden.

enums.name: ContactMethodType
enums.label: Contact method channel
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: Lowercase, and narrower than the slot enum it accompanies (4 channels for 11 slots). See the pairing note on `ContactMethodEnum`.

enums.name: DocumentStatus
enums.label: Document version sighted
enums.controlRationale: ≤3 options — show them all, no click to discover them

enums.name: DocumentType
enums.label: Identification document type
enums.controlRationale: 13–60 options — needs type-to-filter, but the full list is still renderable
hazards: 51 values — the longest enum outside `CountryCode`, and the one most worth grouping in the UI (licences, passports, birth/citizenship, government cards, bank instruments, statements, references) rather than presenting as a flat alphabetical list.
Values are PascalCase identifiers, not display strings: `DriversLicenceAust`, `GovtIssueFinancialBenNot`. They need a label map before a human sees them.

enums.name: ExpenseType
enums.label: Expense type
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: Overlaps `LiabilityName` by name (Credit Card, Home Loan, Personal Loan, Car Loan). The same real-world commitment can be captured as a Contact expense *and* an Opportunity liability; the enums do not stop you double-counting it.

enums.name: IncomeType
enums.label: Income type
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: Also the de-facto vocabulary for `OtherIncomeLineItem.type` on the extension route, where the field is an open string rather than this enum — same options, no validation.

enums.name: OpportunityCategory
enums.label: Opportunity category
enums.controlRationale: 13–60 options — needs type-to-filter, but the full list is still renderable
hazards: Carried by the field named `transactionType`, not `category`. The similarly-named `tranxType` field is a *different* enum (`OpportunityTranxType`). Two adjacent fields, near-identical names, unrelated value sets — the single easiest field pair in this API to wire up backwards.

enums.name: OpportunityTranxType
enums.label: Transaction type
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: Carried by `tranxType`. See the naming collision noted on `OpportunityCategory`.

enums.name: LoanStatusActive
enums.label: Pipeline stage (active)
values: 2. Strategy Appointment Booked & Client Center Portal Send to Clients
5. Loan Proposal Sent to Client Via Email
enums.controlRationale: Overrides the 27-option default (`combobox`): the field this describes is free text on the wire, so the control has to accept values outside the list.
hazards: Not an API constraint. `Opportunity.status` is a free-text string in the contract; these 27 values are the branch's live pipeline catalog. A closed dropdown here will block a legitimate value the moment the branch adds a stage — offer the known list, allow free text.

Five values contain an en-dash (`–`), not a hyphen: `1. Lead – Discovery`, `8.2 Settled – Commission Paid`, `8.3 Construction Loan – Progress Payments`, `9.3/9.4/9.5 Mortgage Review – NN Month`. Retyping them with a hyphen produces a string that will not match.
The leading numbers order the pipeline but do not sort lexically (`10` would fall between `1.` and `2.`); sort on an explicit index, not the label.

enums.name: LoanStatusInactive
enums.label: Pipeline stage (closed)
enums.controlRationale: Overrides the 3-option default (`radio`): the field this describes is free text on the wire, so the control has to accept values outside the list.
hazards: Same free-text caveat as the active list. Numbering jumps from `9.5` straight to `12` — stages 10 and 11 are absent from the catalog, so don't infer the set from the numbering.

enums.name: FinhubContactCategoryName
enums.label: Contact category
enums.controlRationale: Overrides the 15-option default (`combobox`): the field this describes is free text on the wire, so the control has to accept values outside the list.
hazards: Branch data, not a contract constraint — `Category.categoryName` is free text.

Three families share the list: `PREF - *` (comms preference), `FREQ - *` (contact frequency), `REVIEW - *` (review cadence). Group by prefix; a contact holds several at once, so this is a multi-select over `Contact.categories[]`, not a single choice.

enums.name: HousingSituation
enums.label: Housing situation
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: Appears on `Address.housingSituation` (writable) and again on `RelatedParty.housingSituation`, where it is a hydrated read-only copy — rendering an editable control on the RelatedParty copy invites an edit that goes nowhere.

enums.name: RelatedPartyRelationship
enums.label: Relationship to the deal
enums.controlRationale: 13–60 options — needs type-to-filter, but the full list is still renderable
hazards: `JSG/ PRE` carries a space after the slash. It is the literal wire value; normalising the whitespace breaks the match.
Mixes applicant roles (Primary applicant, Co-Applicant, Joint Borrower) with professional roles (Conveyancer, Solicitor, Accountant) in one flat list — worth grouping in the UI.

enums.name: AssetName
enums.label: Asset name
enums.controlRationale: 13–60 options — needs type-to-filter, but the full list is still renderable
hazards: Pairs with `AssetLiabilityType`: `Real Estate` implies type `realEstate`, `Motor Vehicle` implies `vehicle`, the account-shaped names (Cheque Account, Savings Account, Term Deposit, Cash Management) imply `account`. Derive the type from the name and let it be overridden rather than asking twice.

enums.name: ValueBasis
enums.label: Basis of valuation
enums.controlRationale: ≤3 options — show them all, no click to discover them

enums.name: RealEstatePurpose
enums.label: Property purpose
enums.controlRationale: ≤3 options — show them all, no click to discover them

enums.name: LiabilityName
enums.label: Liability name
enums.controlRationale: 13–60 options — needs type-to-filter, but the full list is still renderable
hazards: `Credit Card` and `Store Card` are the only values for which `creditCardType` and `limit` are meaningful — gate those fields on the name.

enums.name: CreditCardType
enums.label: Card scheme
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: Only meaningful when `Liability.name` is `Credit Card`; otherwise it should not be shown or sent.

enums.name: ContactWebhookSubscriptionType
enums.label: Contact webhook scope
values: Contacts where I am the relationship manager
enums.controlRationale: ≤3 options — show them all, no click to discover them
hazards: Values are full sentence-case phrases (`Contacts in my branch/office`), not slugs. They are the wire values — send them verbatim.

enums.name: ContactWebhookEvent
enums.label: Contact webhook event
enums.controlRationale: ≤3 options — show them all, no click to discover them
hazards: `Created or updated` is a single value, not two — it is not a multi-select over `Created` and an update event.

enums.name: OpportunityWebhookSubscriptionType
enums.label: Opportunity webhook scope
values: Opportunities where I am the agent
Opportunities where I am the admin/supervisor
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance

enums.name: OpportunityWebhookEvent
enums.label: Opportunity webhook event
enums.controlRationale: 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance
hazards: Superset of the contact event list: adds `Opportunity Status Changed`, which has no contact-side equivalent.

fieldHazards.note: Observed in GET responses. Strip it at the wire boundary: never bind it to a control, never log it, never put it in client state. It should not exist in any model a UI can reach.

Typed `number | string` — live payloads return Unix epoch milliseconds where the original spec promised a date-time string. A date control must normalise on read (`typeof v === 'number' ? new Date(v) : new Date(String(v))`); passing an epoch number to a string date parser yields Invalid Date silently.
Typed `boolean | string` — Mercury sometimes serialises it as the string `"true"`. A checkbox bound straight to it treats `"false"` as truthy.
String, not number — unlike every other money field in the API (`Expense.amount`, `Income.amount`, `Asset.value` are all numbers). A shared money input must serialise back to a string on these two.

The same concept ships under two casings depending on the endpoint. `Contact.Identification` (capital I) is the Swagger name; live Contact payloads use `identifications`. Read both, write the one the endpoint you are calling expects, and never let a form bind to only one.

Returned by GET as display/hydrated values. `Asset.motorVehicleMake` in particular is display-only — the make is written through `Asset.details`. Render these read-only; an editable control produces an edit that is silently discarded.
Missing the `l` in `Vehicle`. It is the real wire name — correcting the spelling in a client sends a field Mercury ignores.

A JSON-encoded string, not structured JSON, and its PUT is a destructive full replace. A form editing one line item must parse the string, merge, re-stringify and submit the complete array — anything omitted is deleted without warning.
`search=true` is required on collection reads; `count` (default 100) and `offset` (default 0) drive pagination. A list view that omits `search` gets an error, not an empty page.
